blocks.text: 3rd Degree
The Ceremony of Raising to the Third Degree (in the Second Degree)
(The Senior Deacon should be ready to prompt all answers throughout the ceremony.)
W. M. (addressing the Lodge)

Brethren, Bro. A. B. is this day a Candidate to be raised to the sublime Degree of Master Mason; but it is necessary that he should first give proof of his proficiency in the two Degrees through which he has already passed. I will therefore proceed to ask him the usual questions.
Brother Deacons, you will present the Candidate.

(The S.D. waits for J.D. to approach him, then together salute the W.M. in passing in the East and take the Candidate in S.E. and conduct him to the centre of the Lodge underneath the ‘G’. J.D. on the left and S.D. on the right of Candidate, both Deacons stand one pace back from the Candidate.)
W. M. (addresses Can.)
How were you prepared to be passed to the Second Degree?

CAN. - In a manner somewhat similar to that in the First Degree, but with this difference, I was not divested of money nor metals of value; I had my left arm, my left breast, and right knee, made bare, and my left heel slip shod.
W. M. - Upon what were you admitted?
CAN. - Upon the Square.
W. M. - What is a Square?
CAN. - An angle of ninety degrees, or the fourth part of a circle.
W. M. - What are the peculiar objects of research in this Degree?
CAN. - The hidden mysteries of Nature and Science.
W. M. - Where did our antient Brethren go to receive their wages?
CAN. - To the Middle Chamber of King Solomon’s Temple.
W. M. - How did they receive them?
CAN. - Without scruple, and without diffidence.
W. M. - Why in this peculiar manner?
CAN. - Without scruple, knowing themselves to be entitled to receive them; and without diffidence, from the confidence they had in the integrity of their employers in those days.
W. M. - What are the names of those two Great Pillars which stood at the Porchway or Entrance of King Solomon Temple ?
CAN. - That on the left Boaz; that on the right Jachin.
W. M. - What are their separate and conjoint significations?

CAN. - The former denotes in strength; the latter to establish; and when conjoined, stability. For according to our traditions, God said, ‘In Strength I will Establish this My house, that it may stand firm for ever.’
W. M. - Do you seriously pledge me your word of honour as a man, and your fidelity as a Freemason, that you will steadily persevere through the ceremony of being raised to the Third Degree?
CAN. - I do.
W. M. - Do you likewise pledge yourself that you will conceal that which I am about to impart to you with the same strict caution as the other Secrets in Freemasonry?
CAN. - I do.
W. M. - Then I will entrust you with a test of merit, which consists of a Pass Grip and a Pass Word leading from the Second to the Third Degree.
Before I do, I request all F.Cs. to retire under the direction of W. Bro. Asst. Director of Ceremonies.
W. M. (while F.C. passes the J.W.)
Bro. J.W., (J.W. rises with step and sign of F.C.) you will pass out our F.Cs. (J.W. discharges sign and sits)

A.D. of C. - (F.C. is conducted to N.W. corner of Lodge and placed facing East.) You will salute the W.M. as a F.C. taking your time from me. (A.D. of C. salutes the W.M. with step and sign of F.C., ensuring that the F.C. does so at the same time.)
J.W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. rises with step and sign of F.C.) you will pass out our F.Cs.
(I.G. discharges sign and goes to open the door. The F.C. is turned anti-clockwise and conducted to the door where the Tyler waits to receive him)

(Can. is conducted to the N.E. corner of the Lodge and placed facing South. W.M. comes down from the dais and stands in front of Can. facing North.) W. M. - The Pass Grip is given by a distinct pressure between the second and third knuckle joints of the right hand. (W.M. demonstrates to Can.) The Pass Word is Tubal Cain. (W.M. repeats word and Can. follows) Tubal Cain was the first artificer in metals and the import of the word is worldly possessions. This Pass Grip and Pass Word you will be required to give to the Inner Guard on your return to the Lodge. You will now retire, in order to be prepared for the Third Ceremony. Pass Tubal Cain, Worldly Possessions. (W.M. passes Can.’s hand to S.D. and returns to his seat.)
S. D. - (to Can.) You will salute the W.M. in passing as a F.C. (S.D. conducts the Can. past the W.M., South, West to the N.W. corner of the Lodge and places the Can. on his left, both facing East.)
W. M. - (while S.D. and Can. pass the J.W.) Bro. J.W., (J.W. rises with step and sign of F.C.) you will pass out our Candidate. (J.W. discharges sign and sits.)
S. D. - You will salute the W.M. as a F.C. taking your time from me. (S.D. hands his wand to J.D. and salutes the W.M. with step and sign of a F.C., ensuring that the Can. does so at the same time.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. rises with step and sign of F.C.) you will pass out our F.C.
(I.G. discharges sign and goes to open the door. S.D. turns anti- clockwise with Can. and conducts him to the door where the Tyler receives Can.)
The Ceremony of Opening the Lodge in the Third Degree.
(The W. M. gives one knock which is answered by the Wardens, and rises)
W. M. - Brethren, assist me to open the Lodge in the Third Degree. (All rise.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, what is the first care of every Master Mason?
J. W. - To see that the Lodge is properly tyled.
W. M. - you will direct that duty to be done.
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, you will see that the Lodge is properly tyled.
(The I.G. opens the door, looks out and closes the door.)
I. G. (with step and sign of F.C. )
Bro. Junior Warden, the Lodge is properly tyled.
J. W. (with step and sign of F.C. )
Worshipful Master, the Lodge is properly tyled.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, what is our next care ?
S. W. - To see that the Brethren appear to order as Craftsmen.
W. M. - Brethren, to order in the Second Degree. (All stand to order.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, are you a Master Mason?
J. W. - I am, Worshipful Master; try me and prove me.
W. M. - By what instruments in Architecture will you be proved?
J. W. - By the Square and Compasses.
W. M. - Being yourself acquainted with the proper mode, you will prove the Brethren to be Master Masons by signs, and will demonstrate that proof to me by copying their example.
J. W. - Brethren, it is the Worshipful Master's command that you prove yourselves Master Masons by signs.
(All the Brethren present will prove themselves as M.M. except the W.M. and J.W.)
J. W. - Worshipful Master, the Brethren have proved themselves Master Masons by signs, and in obedience to your command I thus copy their example. (Gives step and signs of M.M.)
W. M. - I acknowledge the correctness of the proof. (Gives step and signs of M.M.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, whence come you?
J. W. - From the East, Worshipful Master.
W. M. - Whither directing your course, Bro. Senior Warden?
S. W. - Towards the West.
(The W.M. addresses the remaining questions as follows, alternately to the J.W. and the S.W., without naming them.)
W. M. - What inducement have you to leave the East and to go to the West. ,
J. W. - To seek for that which was lost, and which by your instruction and our own endeavours we hope to find.
W. M. - What is that which was lost?
S. W. - The genuine secrets of a Master Mason.
W. M. - How came they lost?
J. W. - By the untimely death of the Grand Master, Hiram Abif, who lost his life rather than betray the Secrets reposed in him.
W. M. - Where do you hope to find them?
S. W. - Upon the centre.
W. M. - What is a centre?
J. W. - That point within a circle from which every part of the circumference is equally distant.
W. M. - And why upon the centre?
S. W. - Because that is a point from which a Master Mason cannot materially err.
W. M. - Then, Brethren, we will assist you to repair that loss, and may the blessing of The Most High rest upon our united endeavours. So Mote It Be.
W. M. - Brethren, I declare the Lodge duly opened upon the centre, for the purposes of Freemasonry in the Third Degree.

(The knocks are given and answered. The I.P.M. in processional order with the two Deacons goes up to the Master’s pedestal, opens the V.S.L. and arranges the Square and Compasses. Both points of the Compasses are disclosed.)
W. M. - Brethren, observe me.
All Brethren - (All brethren give the Grand and Royal sign)
All glory to The Most High.
W. M. - Brethren, be seated.

blocks.text: The Ceremony of Raising to the Third Degree ( 1st Part )
(All lights are switched off. Only the candle on the W.M.’s pedestal is lighted. The Tyler conducts the Can. to the door, and gives the * ** knocks of the Second Degree as an Alarm.)
I. G. - (advances with step and sign of M.M.) Bro. Junior Warden, there is an alarm. (I.G. discharges sign.)
J. W. - (rises with step and sign of M.M.) Worshipful Master, there is an alarm. (J.W. holds sign)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, you will inquire who seeks admission. (J.W. discharges sign and sits down)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. responds with and holds sign of M.M.) you will see who seeks admission.
(I.G. discharges sign, opens the door, and addresses the Tyler.)
I. G. - Whom have you here?

TY. - Bro. A.B., who has been regularly initiated into Freemasonry, and passed to the Second Degree, and has made such progress therein as he hopes will entitle him to be raised to the Sublime Degree of Master Mason, for which Ceremony he is properly prepared.
I. G. - How does he hope to obtain the privileges of the Third Degree?
TY. - By the Help of God, the united aid of the Square and the Compasses and the benefit of a Pass Word. I. G. (to Can.)
You will give me the Pass Word. (Can. gives the Pass Grip and Pass Word. The I.G. closes the door.)
I. G. (advances with step and sign of M.M., and holds the sign)

Worshipful Master, at the door of the Lodge stands Bro. A. B., who has been regularly initiated into Freemasonry, and been passed to the Second Degree, and now comes properly prepared to be raised to the Sublime Degree of Master Mason.
W. M. - How does he hope to obtain the privileges of the Third Degree?
I. G. - By the Help of God, the united aid of the Square and the Compasses, and the benefit of a Pass Word.
W. M. - We acknowledge the powerful aid by which he seeks admission; do you, Bro. Inner Guard, vouch that he is in possession of the Pass Word ?
I. G. - I do, Worshipful Master.
W. M. - Then let him be admitted in due form. (I.G. discharges sign.)
(The S.D. walks via the East, South and joined by the J.D. together goes to the door. I.G. opens the door.)

I. G. - Bro. A.B, you will advance to me with the step and sign of an E.A. (Can. does so) You will now advance to me with the step and sign of a F.C. (Can. does so. I.G. applies both Points of the Compasses on both breasts, raises the Compasses above his own head to show that he has done so and steps back to behind the S.W.’s chair. S.D. takes the Can.’s right hand in his own left with the J.D. on the left side of the Can., leads Can. to the N.W. corner.)
W. M. - Let the Candidate kneel, while the blessing of Heaven is invoked in aid of our proceedings.
(The Can. kneels and places right hand over his left breast, the Deacons stand one on either side, with their wands crossed so as to meet over the head of the Candidate.)
W. M. - (W.M. knocks once, follow by S.W. and J.W.)
To order, Brethren. (All stand with sign of fidelity.)

Chaplain - Almighty and Eternal God, Architect and Ruler of the Universe, at Whose creative fiat all things were first made, we, the frail creatures of Thy providence, humbly implore Thee to pour down upon this convention, assembled in Thy Holy Name, the continual dew of Thy Blessing. More especially we beseech Thee to impart Thy grace to this Thy servant, who now seeks to participate with us, in the Secrets and Mysteries of a Master Mason. Indue him with such fortitude, that in the hour of trial he fail not, but that
passing safely under Thy protection through the ‘Valley of the Shadow of Death’, he may finally arise from the tomb of transgression to shine as the stars for evermore. So Mote It Be.
W. M. - Let the Candidate rise and perambulate the Lodge. (W.M. knocks once, follow by S.W. and J.W.)

(S.D. conducts the Can. up the North with J.D. following behind Can.; S.D. instructs him to salute the W.M. in passing, without stopping, as an E.A., and takes him to the front of the J.W., and instructs him to advance with the Step and the Sign of an E.A.; J.W. responds by rising with step and sign of E.A.)
J. W. - Do you bring anything else?
CAN. - I do. (S.D. directs Can. to give the Grip of an E.A. to J.W.)
J. W. - What is this?
CAN. - The Grip or Token of an Entered Apprentice Freemason.
J. W. - What does this Grip demand?
CAN. - A Word.
J. W. - Give me that Word, and being lawfully demanded in open Lodge, you may give it freely and in full.
CAN. - Boaz.
J. W. - Pass Boaz. (J.W. passes Can.’s hand to S.D. and sits.)

(S.D. conducts the Can. down South and West, and instructs him to salute the S.W. in passing as an E.A. In the second perambulation, Can. is instructed to salute the W.M. and the J.W. in passing as F.Cs. The Can. is halted in front of the S.W., and instructed to advance with the Step and the Sign of a F.C.; S.W. responds by rising with step and sign of F.C.)
S. W. - Have you anything further to communicate?
CAN. - I have. (Gives the Grip of a F.C.)
S. W. - What is this?
CAN. - The Grip or Token of a Fellow-Craft Freemason.
S. W. - What does this Grip demand?
CAN. - A Word.
S. W. - Give me the Word and being lawfully demanded in open Lodge, you may give it freely and in full.
CAN. - Jachin.
S. W. - Pass, Jachin. (S.W. passes Can.’s right hand to S.D. and sits.)
(S.D. conducts the Can. to the N.W. corner of the Lodge, facing East. S.D. taps the floor once with his wand. The W.M. gives one knock, which is answered by the Wardens.)

W. M. - The Brethren in the North, East, South and West will take notice that Bro. A. B. is about to pass in view before them, to show that he is properly prepared to be raised to the Sublime Degree of Master Mason.
(In the third perambulation, all three salute the W.M., and the J.W. in passing as F.Cs. The Can. is halted in front of the S.W.)
S. D. - You will advance to the S.W. with the step and sign of a F.C. and be prepared to give the Pass Grip and Pass Word
leading from the second to the third degree which were communicated to you before you retired from the Lodge.
(Can. advances with the Step and the Sign of a F.C.; S.W. responds by rising with step and sign of F.C.)
S. W. - Do you bring anything further?
CAN. - I do. (Instructed by the S.D. he gives the Pass Grip)
S. W. - What is this?
CAN. - The Pass Grip leading from the Degree of Fellow-Craft to that of Master Mason. S. W. - To this is attached a Pass Word, which I will thank you for.
CAN. - Tubal Cain.
S. W. - Who was Tubal Cain ?
CAN. - The first Artificer in Metals.
S. W. - What is the import of the Word ?
CAN. - Worldly Possession.
W. M. - Pass Tubal Cain, Worldly Possession. (S.W. passes Can.’s right hand to S.D. and sits.)
(S.D. conducts Can. to the left of the S.W. facing East. S.W. takes the Can.'s right hand in his own left, and rises with sign of fidelity.)
S. W. - Worshipful Master, I present to you Bro. A. B., a Candidate properly prepared to be raised to the Sublime Degree of Master Mason.

W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, your presentation shall be attended to, for which purpose you will direct the Deacons to instruct the Candidate to advance to the East by the proper Steps. (S.W. sits and returns Can.’s hand to S.D.)
S. W. - Bro. Deacons, it is the Worshipful Master's command that you instruct the Candidate to advance to the East by the proper Steps.
(S.D. conducts Can. to N./N.E. of the Lodge, facing South.)

S. D. - (to Can.) The method of advancing from West to East in this Degree is by Seven Steps, the first Three are as though one were Stepping over a Grave; the remaining four others are ordinary Walking Steps. First I will demonstrate, then you will copy me.

(S.D. demonstrates, then places Can. at the brink of the grave, takes Can.’s hand and guides him through the 7 steps ending in front of the W.M.’s pedestal . On completion, they are joined by the J.D. on the Can.’s left.)

W. M. - (to Can.) You are now required to enter into a very serious and Solemn Obligation, to be followed by a greater trial of your fortitude and fidelity than any you have yet experienced. Are you prepared to meet them in a becoming spirit?
CAN. - I am.
W. M. - You will Knee on Both Knees, place both hands upon the Volume of the Sacred Law and say after me:

(The W.M. rises and gives one Knock, which is answered by the Wardens. The W.M. and all the Brethren rise, and stand to order with the sign of fidelity. The Deacons cross wands over the head of the Can.)

W. M. - I, A.B., in the presence of The Most High and of this Worthy and Worshipful Lodge of Master Masons, lawfully constituted and regularly assembled, hereby (W.M. touches Can.’s right hand with his right hand) and hereon (W.M. touches the V.S.L. with his right hand and returns back to sign of fidelity) most solemnly and sincerely swear, that I will always hele, conceal, and never wilfully reveal any or either of the secrets or mysteries, of, or at all belonging to, this Third Degree in Freemasonry, denominated the Master Masons' Degree, to any individual whomsoever, except it be to one who has been regularly initiated into Freemasonry, and passed to the Second Degree, and after a full month's probation has been presented as a Candidate properly prepared and fully qualified to be admitted to this Degree, and then only in the body of a Master Masons' Lodge regularly opened upon the centre. I further solemnly promise to adhere to the principles of the Square and the Compasses as they are inculcated in the First and the Second Degree; and that I will observe and uphold the Five Points Of Fellowship in act as well as in word; that my Hand given to a Freemason shall be a sure pledge of Brotherhood; that my Feet shall travel - if necessary - through dangers and difficulties, to unite with his, in forming a base upon which we two, standing side by side, may figuratively represent a column of mutual defence and support; that my Knee bent in daily prayer to The Most High shall always remind me of a Brother's wants, and shall dispose my heart to succour him in his weakness, and to relieve his necessities, as far as may fairly be done without injury to myself or my connections; that my Breast shall be the safe and sacred repository of his secrets, when entrusted to me as secrets, save that murder, treason, felony, and all other offences contrary to the Ordinances of God, and the Laws of the Land, shall be always especially excepted; and finally, that I will maintain a Freemason's honour and will carefully preserve it as my own; that I will not injure or malign him myself; nor knowingly suffer others to do so, if in my power to prevent it, but on the contrary will boldly repel the slanderer of his good name, and will at all times, and in all ways, most strictly respect the chastity of those nearest and dearest to him, in the persons of his wife, his sister, and his child. These several points I solemnly swear to observe, without evasion, equivocation, or mental reservation. of any kind, and I pray to the Most High that He will keep me steadfast, in this, the Great and Solemn Obligation of a Master Mason.

W. M. - As a pledge of your fidelity to this Solemn Obligation which shall be binding upon you for as long as you shall live, I call upon you to Seal it upon the Volume of the Sacred Law three times with your Lips. (Can. kisses the V.S.L. three times. The Deacons uncross their wands and all Brethren discharge sign of fidelity.)

W. M. - Let me once more, and for the last time, direct your attention to the relative positions of the Square and the Compasses. When you were made an Entered Apprentice, both points were concealed; (W.M. points to but does not touch the Square and Compasses.) in the Second Degree, one was disclosed; now both are exhibited, implying that you are now at liberty to work with both points of the Compasses, in order to render the Circle of your Masonic duties complete. (Takes him by both hands.) Rise, duly Obligated Probationer in the Third Degree. (Passes hands to S.D.)

(The Can. is taken a few paces back until his heels are at the edge of the grave with the J.D. to his left and the S.D. to his right. M.M. comes to the East/North-East besides the W.M.’s pedestal and salutes the W.M. with sign of fidelity, then turns to face the Can.)

M. M. - Now that you have taken the great and solemn Obligation of a Master Mason, I will shortly proceed to subject you to that last and greatest trial, by which alone you can be admitted to participation in the Secrets of the Third Degree. But it is first my duty to direct your attention to retrospect of those Degrees through which you have already passed, by which you will be enabled the better to comprehend and to appreciate the connection of our whole system and the interdependence of its several parts. Your initiation into Freemasonry in a state of helpless Indigence was an emblematical representation of the entrance of all men upon this their mortal existence. It inculcated the useful lessons of natural equality and mutual dependence; it instructed you, in the active exercise of Charity - in administering relief and consolation to your fellow - creatures in the time of their affliction that it is in very deed and in truth ‘more blessed to give than to receive.’ But, above all, it taught you to bend with humility and resignation to the will of The

Great Architect Of The Universe, and to dedicate your heart, thus purified from every baleful and malignant passion, and fitted for the reception of Moral Truth, Wisdom, and Virtue, to the service of God, and to the good of your fellow-men. Proceeding onward, and still guiding your steps by the Principles of Moral Truth, you were led in the Second Degree to contemplate the Intellectual Faculties, and to trace them, from their inception and development, through the paths of Heavenly Science, even to the Throne of God Himself. The Secrets of Nature and the Principles of intellectual and Scientific Truth were then permitted to be unveiled to your view. To your mind, thus cultured and matured by Virtue and Science, Nature herself presents one great and useful lesson more. She prepares you by contemplation for the closing hour of your existence; and when you shall have been conducted through the ‘manifold changes and chances of this mortal life,’ she finally instructs you how to die. This, my Brother, is the peculiar object of the Third Degree in Freemasonry. It invites us to reflect upon this awful subject, and teaches us to feel that to the just and upright man Death has no terrors equal to the stain of falsehood and dishonour. Of this great truth the Annals of Freemasonry afford a glorious example in the unshaken fidelity and noble - of an antient Grand Master of our Order Hiram Abif who was treacherously and cruelly slain, shortly before the completion of King Solomon Temple in the designing and construction of which he was - as our traditions inform us - the chief architect. In order that you may be enabled to ‘comprehend and to appreciate’ the remaining portion of the Ceremony, I will explain to you the meaning of the word Abif which I have just used in connection with the name Hiram. It is a Hebrew word signifying ‘the son of a widow.’ It is recorded in the Volume of the Sacred Law that, in accordance with the request of King Solomon, Hiram, King of Tyre, sent to him a man who was well skilled in all details connected with ‘the erection of stately and superb edifices,’ to assist King Solomon in designing, erecting, beautifying, and adorning the Temple at Jerusalem. This man is described in the Volume of the Sacred Law as ‘the son of a widow woman of Tyre,’ and his name, like that of the King of Tyre, was Hiram.

These two antient worthies - both bearing the same name, and both being at that time (in conjunction with King Solomon) Grand Masters in our Order - are mentioned in various portions of the annals of Freemasonry, sometimes separately, sometimes in juxtaposition; and in order to distinguish between the two, we call the one Hiram, King of Tyre, the other Hiram Abif, that is Hiram the son of the widow. We shall recur to this latter designation at a later period in the ceremony. (M.M. salutes the W.M. with sign of fidelity and takes his seat.)

(The S.W. hiding the Level behind him and the J.W. hiding the Plump Rule behind him, take up their positions. S.W. to the left of J.D. in the North and J.W. to the right of S.D. in the South. All four together with the Can. forming a straight line facing East. W.M. hiding the Heavy Maul behind him, takes up position in front of and facing Can.)

W. M. - I will now narrate to you the circumstances which led to the assassination of the Grand Master Hiram Abif, the chief architect of the Temple, the first martyr to his fidelity as a Master Mason, of whom the annals of Freemasonry contain the record; and I will then describe to you the manner of his death, in accordance with the teaching of our Masonic traditions. Five Fellow-Crafts, of the Order of the Menatschim - that higher Order whose members were appointed to superintend the labours of those craftsmen and others who wrought in the building of the Temple - seeing that that great and holy work was nearly completed, and that they and their fellows were not yet admitted to participation in the secrets, and thereby entitled to the privileges, of the Third Degree, joined in a conspiracy to obtain those secrets by any means, even if it should be necessary to have recourse to violence. On the eve, however, of carrying their plot into execution, two of them relented (the 2 Deacons take one pace backward); but the remaining three, being of a more determined and ruthless character than the seceding two, still persevered in their atrocious design, in the prosecution of which they placed themselves respectively at the South (the J.D. takes one loud step forward and places himself facing North and at right angle to the Can.), the North (the S.D. takes one loud step forward and places himself facing South and at right angle to the Can.), and the East (the W.M. takes one loud step forward facing the Can.) entrances of the Temple, whither the Grand Master, Hiram Abif, had gone to offer up his prayers and thanksgiving to The Most High, as was his wonted custom at the hour of offering the Evening Sacrifice. His devotions being ended, he. attempted to return by the South door, where the first conspirator was posted, and who, for want of other weapon, had armed himself with a heavy Plumb-rule. Assuming a threatening demeanour (the J.D. places his left hand on the Can.’s right shoulder and assume a threatening stance by holding the plump rule high up and staring at the Can.), he demanded of the Chief Architect the secrets of the Third Degree, warning him that death would be the consequence of a refusal. But he, true to his Obligation, replied, that those Secrets were known but to Three in the world, namely, to Solomon King of Israel, to Hiram King of Tyre, and himself, and that without the consent and co-operation of the other two, he would not - and indeed could not - reveal them; but he assured him that diligence and patience would, in due time, entitle the worthy Craftsman to participation in those Secrets, but that for himself he would rather suffer death than he would improperly reveal them. This answer failing to satisfy his assailant, he struck a heavy blow at the head of the Grand Master, but missing his aim, the weapon glanced with such force upon his Right Temple (the J.W. strikes his own left hand with the Plump Rule over the Can.’s right temple. Immediately the J.D. kicks the back of the Can.’s left knee.), as to cause him to sink to the ground upon his Left Knee. Recovering from this shock (Can. is lifted up), he then made for the North door, where the second ruffian was posted, to whom he answered, as in the previous instance, with undiminished firmness, when the villain, who was armed with a Level, struck him a violent blow upon the Left Temple (the S.W. strikes his own left hand with the Level over the Can.’s left temple. Immediately the S.D. kicks the back of the Can.’s right knee.), which caused him to sink to the ground upon his Right Knee. Finding all hope of escape cut off at both these quarters (Can. is lifted up), the stricken man then staggered, faint and bleeding, to the East door, where the third conspirator was posted. On receiving a similar reply to his insolent demand - for even at this perilousmoment the firmness of the Chief Architect remained unshaken - the murderous ruffian, who was armed with a heavy Maul, struck him a violent blow full (the W.M. strikes the Can.’s forehead with the Heavy Maul) upon the Forehead which laid him lifeless at his feet. (the Can. is made to lie down in the ‘grave’.)

W. M. - The Brethren will take notice that in the recent Ceremony, as well as in his present position, our Brother has been made to represent one of the brightest characters recorded in the annals of Freemasonry, namely, Hiram Abif, who during his active and useful life excelled in all the curious and masterly workmanship of his Craft; and by his death, which he nobly suffered rather than he would betray the Secrets entrusted to his keeping, he has left an example worthy of the imitation of Freemasons through all succeed- ing ages. This, we trust, will make such an impression upon his and your minds, that you will not fail to act with similar firmness if you should ever be placed in a similar position of trial.
(Death March to be performed with music.)
(The W.M., S.W. and J.W. maintain step and sign of an E.A. and hold the sign.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, you will endeavour to raise the Body of Hiram Abif with the Grip of an Entered Apprentice.
(The J.W. makes the trial with grip of an E.A., W.M. and S.W. hold sign of E.A.)

(The J.W. holding the sign of E.A., squares the ‘grave’ and as he reaches the N.W. corner, the S.W. also holding sign of E.A., moves across to the J.W.’s former position and the J.W. stops at the S.W.’s former position.)
J. W. - Worshipful Master, it proves a Slip. (The W.M., S.W. and J.W. discharge step and sign of an E.A.)
(The W.M., S.W. and J.W. maintain step and sign of an F.C. and hold the sign.)
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, you will now make trial of the Fellow-Craft's Grip.
(The S.W. makes the trial with grip of a F.C., W.M. and S.W. hold sign of F.C.)

(The S.W. holding the sign of F.C., squares the ‘grave’ and as he reaches the N.W. corner, the J.W. also holding sign of F.C., moves across to his former position and the S.W. stops at his former position.)
S. W. - Worshipful Master, this proves a Slip also. (The W.M., S.W. and J.W. discharge step and sign of F.C.)

W. M. - Bro. Wardens, you have both failed in your endeavours, but there yet remains a peculiar method, namely, the taking a firm and lion-like hold of the sinew of the right arm, and raising our Bro. upon the Five Points Of Fellowship, which, with your assistance, I will now make trial of. (W.M. raises the Can. with the assistance of the S.W. and J.W.) Hand to Hand, Foot to Foot, Knee to Knee, Breast to Breast, and Hand Over Back. It is thus, my Brother, that all Master Masons are raised, from a figurative death to a reunion with the companions of their former labours.
(The W.M. and Wardens resume their Chairs. The S.D. conducts the Can. past the J.W., S.W. and down the North and stops at the brink of the ‘grave’ facing South.)

M. M. - Let me now beg you to observe that the light of a Master Mason is but Darkness Visible, serving fitly to represent that mysterious Veil of Darkness which rests upon the prospects of futurity, and which the eye of human reason cannot penetrate, unless assisted by the Light which cometh from above. By this glimmering ray you may perceive that you stand upon the very brink of the

Grave, into which you just now figuratively Descended, and which, when this transitory life shall have passed away, will again Receive You into its Cold Bosom. Let the Emblems of Mortality which lie before you remind you of your inevitable destiny, and guide your contemplation to the most interesting of all human studies, the knowledge of yourself. Be careful to perform your allotted task while it is yet day, ‘the night cometh when no man can work’; continue to listen to the voice of reason, and to the testimony of Revelation, both of which bear witness that in this perishable frame dwells a vital and immortal principle, inspiring a holy confidence that the Lord of Life will enable us finally to trample the King of Terrors under our feet, and to lift our eyes to Him in Whose hands alone are ‘the issues of Life and Death,’ and in whose mercy we trust for the fulfilment of his gracious promises of Peace and Salvation to the faithful and obedient of the human race.
(The I.G. switches on the lights. The candles on the pedestals of W.M., S.W. and J.W. are lit.)
(The S.D. instructs the Can. to step backwards to the North East corner facing South.)

sections.heading: Signs and the five points of fellowship

blocks.text: W. M. - Now that you have passed through the necessary preliminary ordeal, I will proceed to entrust you with the Secrets of this degree. You will first advance to me with the Step (the shortest possible, a few inches only), and the Sign of an Entered Apprentice. (Can. does so and W.M. responds likewise.) Now, again, as a Fellow-Craft. (Can. does so and W.M. responds likewise.) Retaining the Sign of a Fellow-Craft, you will now take another Short Pace as before. (W.M. instructs Can. and demonstrates by taking a short pace forward with his left foot and put the heel of the right foot into the hollow of the left foot. The Can. does accordingly.)That is the third Regular Step in Freemasonry; and it is in that position that the Secrets of the Third Degree are communicated. They consist, as in the First and Second Degrees, of Signs, Tokens, and Words. The Signs in the whole are five in number, corresponding therein with The Five Points Of Fellowship. Of these, three are ordinary and two are extraordinary. I will at this stage of the Ceremony communicate to you the three ordinary Signs of a Master Mason. Two of these are Casual, the third is the Penal Sign. The first Casual Sign is formed from the F.Cs. thus; by a simultaneous movement you drop the left hand into this position, elevating the right with the back of the hand to the face, shielding the eyes with the head turned over the right shoulder.(W.M. demonstrates and instructs the Can. to copy.) This is called the Sign of Horror, as though struck with Horror at some gruesome object at which you had been gazing. The second is given thus; keeping the body erect, bend the head slightly forward, and pat the forehead with the palm of the hand. (W.M. demonstrates and instructs the Can. to copy.) This called the Sign of Sympathy, as though in sympathy with the sufferings of another. The Third is the Penal Sign. It is given thus; by drawing the hand smartly across the body, dropping it to the side and recovering with the thumb to the navel. (W.M. demonstrates and instructs the Can. to copy.) It alludes to the Ancient and Traditional penalties at one time included in the Obligation in this degree, it implied that, as a man of honour and a Master Mason you would rather be struck in twain, (W.M. demonstrates and Can. copies the motion of the Penal Sign) and have your body burnt to ashes and those ashes scattered over the face of earth and water, by the four cardinal winds of heaven, so that no trace or remembrance of you should longer exist among men, and more particularly among Master Masons than improperly reveal any of the Secrets of this degree. The Grip or Token is the first of the Five Points Of Fellowship, which are thus given and illustrated: Hand to Hand, (W.M. takes Can.’s right hand with the lion-like grip) I greet you as a Brother; Feet to Feet, (W.M. places his right foot against Can.’s right foot)my feet shall travel, if necessary, through dangers and difficult- ies to assist you in your time of need; Knee to Knee, (W.M. places his right knee to touch Can.’s right knee) my knees bent in daily prayer to The Most High, shall always remind me of a Brother's wants; Breast to Breast, (W.M. places his left breast to touch Can.’s left breast) my breast shall be the safe and sacred repository of your lawful Secrets when entrusted to me as Secret; Hand over Back, (W.M. extends his left hand over Can.’s left shoulder, Can. do likewise over the W.M.’s left shoulder) I will maintain a Freemason's honour in his absence as I would if he were present. It is in this Position only, and even then in a whisper, except in open Lodge, that the Words of this Degree are communicated; they are Machaben and Machbinna ; these words signifying severally the Death of the Builder and the Builder is Slain. The Deacons will now conduct you to the Wardens for trial and probation. (W.M. releases the Can., returns him to the S.D. and goes back to his seat.)
(I.P.M. steps down from the dais and faces the Can.)

I. P. M. - As you will shortly be called upon to salute the Worshipful Master in passing as a Master Mason, I will demonstrate the manner of saluting and you will copy my example when called upon to do so. (I.P.M. demonstrates the salute and returns to his seat.)
S. D. - (to Can.) You will salute the Worshipful Master in passing as a Master Mason. (The Can. does accordingly as he is led by the S.D. to the J.W.)
(The S.D. places the Can. facing the J.W., passes his wand to the J.D., places himself facing East and at right angle to the Can. and salutes the J.W. as a M.M. and holding the sign.)
S. D. - Bro. Junior Warden, I present to you Bro. A.B. on being raised to the Sublime Degree of Master Mason. (S.D. discharges sign.)

J. W. - You will advance to me first as an Entered Apprentice, (Can. does so. J.W. rises and reply with step and sign of an E.A.) next as a Fellow-Craft, (Can. does so. J.W. replies with step and sign of an F.C.) and now as a Master Mason. (S.D. demonstrates the 3rd Regular Step and instructs the Can. to copy. J.W. responds with the 3rd Regular Step.)
J. W. - What is that?
CAN. - (prompted by S.D.) The Third Regular Step in Freemasonry.
J. W. - Have you anything to communicate?
CAN. - I have. (S.D. demonstrates the Sign of Horror and Can. copies.)
J. W. - What is that?
CAN. - The Sign of Horror.
J. W. - Do you bring anything further?
CAN. - I do. (S.D. demonstrates the Sign of Sympathy and Can. copies.)
J. W. - What is that?
CAN. - The Sign of Sympathy.
J. W. - Anything further?
CAN. - I do. (S.D. demonstrates the Penal Sign and Can. copies.)
J. W. - What is that?
CAN. - The Penal Sign of a Master Mason.
J. W. - To what does it allude?

CAN. - To the Ancient and Traditional penalties at one time included in the Obligation in this degree, implying that I would rather be struck in twain (S.D. demonstrates and Can. copies the M.M. penal sign) than improperly reveal any of the Secrets of this degree. (J.W. sits down.)
(S.D. retrieves his wand and conducts the Can. to the South West corner of the Lodge and placed him facing North. S.D. passes his wand to the J.D., salutes the S.W. as a M.M. and holding the sign.)
S. D. - Brother Senior Warden, I present to you Bro. A.B. on being raised to the sublime degree of Master Mason. (S.D. discharges sign and retrieves his wand.)
(The S.W. descends from the dais and stand facing the Can. with sufficient space between them.)

S. W. - Brother A.B., you will advance to me with the step and sign of an E.A. (The Can. does accordingly on his own and S.W. responds likewise.) You will now advance to me as a F.C. (The Can. does accordingly and S.W. responds likewise.) Now you will advance to me with the step only of a M.M. (The Can. does accordingly.)
(S.W. goes through the Five Points of Fellowship with Can., naming each, but not explaining them.)
S. W. - Hand to hand, foot to foot, knee to knee, breast to breast, hand over back. Machaben Machbinna – the death of the builder, the builder is slain. (S.W. releases Can. and returns to his seat.)
(S.D. conducts Can. to the left of the S.W. and places him facing East and passes Can.’s hand to the S.W.)
S. W. - (rises with sign of M.M. and holding Can.’s right hand) Worshipful Master, I present to you Bro. A.B. for some further mark of your favour.

W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, I delegate to Bro. M.M. the authority to invest our Brother with the distinguishing Badge of a Master Mason. (S.W. discharges M.M. sign, returns Can.’s hand to S.D. and sits.)
(S.D. conducts Can. to North/North-west and places Can. facing South.)

M. M. (M.M. salutes the W.M. as M.M. and takes the M.M. apron.) - Bro. A. B., by the Worshipful Master's command, I invest you (places M.M. apron on Can. as his F.C. apron is removed) with the distinguishing Badge of a Master Mason, to mark the further progress you have made in the Science. I will add, that the Badge with which you have now been invested not only denotes your rank as a Master Mason, but is likewise intended to remind you of the great duties which you have solemnly engaged to perform; and while it marks your own superiority in the Craft, it calls upon you to afford assistance and instruction to the Brethren in the inferior Degrees. (M.M. salutes the W.M. and takes his seat.)
(The S.D. conducts the Can. along the North side and stops in front of the Secretary’s table and places Can. facing the J.W.)

J. W. - I will now explain to you the Working Tools of this Degree. They are the Skirrett; the Pencil; and the Compasses. (J.W. shows implements as they are named.) The Skirret is an implement which acts upon a centre-pin, from which a line is drawn to mark out the ground for the foundation of the intended structure. With the Pencil the skilful Architect delineates the building in a draft or plan for the instruction and guidance of the workmen. The Compasses enable him to ascertain and determine with accuracy and precision the limits and proportions of its several parts. Those are the uses of these implements in operative masonry; but in this as in the First and Second Degrees, we, not professing to be Operative, but Free and Accepted, or Speculative, Masons, apply these Tools to our morals; and in this sense the Skirret points out to us that straight and undeviating line of conduct marked out for us in the Volume of the Sacred Law.

The Pencil teaches us that all our thoughts, words, and actions are observed and recorded by the Most High, to Whom we must hereafter render an account of our conduct through life. The Compasses remind us of His unerring and impartial justice, in having accurately defined for our instruction the limits of good and evil; and that He will, either reward or punish us according as we have obeyed or disregarded His Divine commands. Thus the Working Tools of this Sublime Degree teach us to bear in mind, and to act according to, the Laws of our Divine Creator, in the hope that when we shall be summoned from this sublunary abode, we may ascend to that Grand Lodge above, where the World's Great Architect lives and reigns supreme. (J.W. salutes W.M. as M.M. and sits.)
(S.D. conducts Can. up the North and East to the front of the W.M.’s pedestal.)
W. M. - You may now retire, in order to be Restored to your usual Comfort, and on your return into the Lodge, the remaining portion of our Traditional History will be narrated to you.
(S.D. places Can. one pace back and instructs Can.)
S. D. - You will salute the W.M. as a M.M. (Can. does so and S.D. conducts the Can. down East, South, West to the N.W. corner of the Lodge and places the Can. on his left, both facing East.)
W. M. - (while S.D. and Can. pass the J.W.) Bro. J.W., (J.W. rises with step and sign of M.M.) you will pass out our Candidate. (J.W. discharges sign and sits.)

S. D. - You will salute the W.M. as a M.M. taking your time from me. (S.D. hands his wand to J.D. and salutes the W.M. with step and sign of a M.M., ensuring that the Can. does so at the same time and then retrieves his wand.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. rises with step and sign of M.M..) you will pass out our Candidate.

(I.G. discharges sign and goes to open the door. S.D. turns anti- clockwise with Can. and conducts him to the door where the Tyler receives Can.) (I.G. closes door and both Deacons return to their respective positions, place their wands in the stands and sit in unison.)
(The Lodge is called off at this stage to allow Brethren to ease themselves.)

blocks.text: Calling the Brethren from Labour to Refreshment.
(The W.M. gives one knock, which is answered by the Wardens.)
W. M. - Principal Officers upstanding.
(The Wardens rise with the W.M.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, (J.W. responds with and holds the sign of E.A.) what time is it?
J. W. - High Noon, Worshipful Master.
W. M. - What is to be done at High Noon?
J. W. - Your Worship's pleasure.
W. M. - Then you will call the Brethren from labour to refreshment.
(J.W. discharges sign of E.A.)

J. W. - Brethren, it is the Worshipful Master's command that you cease from labour and go to refreshment; taking care to keep within hail, so as to be ready to come on again in due time, that profit and pleasure may be the result.
(The J.W. gives one knock, which is repeated by the S.W. and the W.M. The J.W. raises his Column, the S.W. lowers his. The I.P.M. closes the V.S.L., without moving the Square and Compasses.)
Calling the Brethren from Refreshment to Labour.
(The W.M. gives one knock, which is repeated by the Wardens.)
W. M. - Principal Officers upstanding.
(The Wardens rise with the W.M.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, (J.W. responds with and holds the sign of E.A.) what time is it?
J. W. - Past High Noon, Worshipful Master.
W. M. - Then you will call the Brethren from refreshment to labour.
(J.W. discharges sign of E.A.)
J. W. - Brethren, it is the Worshipful Master's command that you cease from refreshment and return to labour, for the further despatch of Masonic business.
(The J.W. gives one knock which is repeated by the S.W. and the W.M. The J.W. lowers his Column, and the S.W. raises his. The I.P.M. reopens the V.S.L.)

sections.heading: The second part and traditional history

blocks.text: The Ceremony of Raising to the Third Degree ( 2nd Part )
(The Can. is restored to his former comforts and wearing a M.M. apron. The Tyler gives the knocks of the 3rd Degree.)
J. W. - (rises with step and sign of a M.M.) Worshipful Master, there is a report. (J.W. holds sign.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, you will inquire who seeks admission. Should it be the return of our newly raised Master Mason, admit him. (J.W. discharges sign and sits down.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. responds and holds sign of a M.M.) you will see who seeks admission. Should it be the return of our newly raised Master Mason, admit him.
(The I.G. discharges sign and opens the door.)
I. G. - (to Tyler) Whom have you there?
TY. - Our newly raised Master Mason.

(The S.D. squares the Lodge via the East, South and joined by the J.D. together goes to the door. The S.D. conducts the Can. to the N.W. corner of the Lodge and places him facing East with right hand over left breast.)
S. D. - You will salute the Worshipful Master with the step and sign of a Master Mason.
(The S.D. conducts the Can. down South and stops at about mid- point between the North-West corner and the Secretary’s table and places him facing South looking towards the S.W.)
(The S.W. rises and salutes the W.M. as a M.M.)
S. W. - (to Deacons) Bro. Deacons, please be seated. (Deacons sit down.)

S. W. - (to Can.) We discontinued the narrative of our Traditional History at that part of it which describes the manner of the Death of the Grand Master, Hiram Abif. A loss so important as that of the Chief Architect could not fail to be speedily and severely felt. The want of those plans and designs which had theretofore been regularly supplied through every department of the work, had given rise to grave apprehensions that some serious mischance must have befallen him. The Menatschim - who were the general Overseers of the work - deputed certain of the more distinguished of their number to crave an audience with King Solomon, and to acquaint him with the utter confusion into which the absence of the Chief Architect had plunged them, and at the same time to express to him their fears that to some dire calamity must be attributed his so sudden and mysterious disappearance. King Solomon thereupon ordered a general muster of the Craftsmen throughout the various departments, when three of the superior class were not to be found; and on the same day the two who had originally joined in the conspiracy went before the King, and made a full confession of all that they knew, up to the time of their withdrawing themselves from the number of the conspirators. The fears of King Solomon being awakened for the safety of the Chief Architect, he selected fifteen trusty Fellow-Crafts, and ordered them to go and make diligent search for the person of the Grand Master, and to ascertain if he were still or had suffered in the attempt to extort from him the Secrets of his superior Degree. Accordingly, a day having been fixed for their return to Jerusalem, they formed themselves into three Fellow-Craft Lodges, consisting of five each, and departed severally from the three entrances of the Temple. Many days were spent in fruitless search; indeed, one Lodge eventually returned to Jerusalem without having effected any discovery; but the Brethren of the Second Lodge were more fortunate, for on the evening of a certain day, they having suffered many privations and much personal fatigue, one of their number, who had rested himself in a reclining position, in order to assist his rising, took hold of a shrub under whose shade he had reclined, and which to his surprise came easily out of the ground. On a close examination of the spot he discovered that the surface had been recently disturbed; he therefore hailed his Brethren, and with their assistance he reopened the ground, and there discovered the body of the Grand Master, very indecently buried. They covered it up with all respect and reverence; and in order to mark the spot they placed a branch of acacia at the head of the grave and then hastened to com- municate the afflicting intelligence to King Solomon. He, when the first emotions of his grief had subsided, ordered them to return, taking with them a sufficient number of Brethren to assist them, and to raise the body of Hiram Abif and to convey it to Jerusalem, there to perform upon it such rites of sepulture as became his rank and exalted talents. At the same time he informed them that by his untimely death the Genuine Secrets of a Master Mason were for a time Lost ; he therefore charged them to be particularly careful to observe any Casual Sign, Token, or Word which might occur while they were engaged in performing this last sad office of respect to departed merit. They performed their task with the utmost fidelity, for, on reopening the grave, one of the Brethren, looking round, observed several standing in this position, as though struck with Horror (sign) at what they beheld; others, viewing the gaping wound still visible on his forehead smote their own thus in Sympathy (sign) with his Sufferings. Two of the Brethren then descended into the grave, and severally attempted to raise the body of the Grand Master by the Grip of an Entered Apprentice and a Fellow-Craft; but as the body had lain some days in the Grave the Flesh gave and Slipped. A third zealous and more expert Brother then descended and taking a Firm and Lion-Like hold on the Sinew of the Right Arm, he, with the assistance of the other two, succeeded in raising him on the Five Points Of Fellowship and while some looked on in speechless Grief, others more animated exclaimed, Machaben and Machbinna, these Words signifying severally the Death of the Builder and the Builder is Slain. These Casual Signs, Grip, and Words were duly reported to King Solomon, who whereupon ordered that they should serve to distinguish them and all Master Masons throughout the World, until time or circumstances should restore the genuine ones. It only remains for me to account for the Third Lodge of Craftsmen. They had pursued their researches in the direction of Joppa, and were meditating a return to Jerusalem, when, on passing the mouth of a cavern, they heard issuing therefrom sounds of lamentation and remorse. On entering to ascertain the cause, they found three men who appeared to answer the description of those who were missing, and who on being charged with the murder, and finding all chance of escape cut off, made a full confession of their guilt. They were then Bound and Led to Jerusalem, where King Solomon ordered them to immediate execution, a punishment which the heinousness of their crime richly merited. The Body of Hiram Abif was ordered to be Reburied near to, but without, the walls of Jerusalem. He could not be buried within the precincts of the Temple, nor even within the City, because during the forty years' wanderings of the Israelites in the Wilderness, they, by God's special command, buried their dead beyond (or outside) the limits of the Camp; and when they entered into the Promised Land, and dwelt in fenced cities, they always buried their dead without the walls of their several cities. The fifteen Trusty Fellow-Crafts who had assisted in searching and finding the body of the Grand Master and in bringing his murderers to justice, were ordered to conduct his obsequies, clothed in White Aprons as emblems of their innocence. The implements with which Hiram Abif was Slain are the Plump Rule, the Level, and the Heavy Maul. The Skull and Cross Bones the emblems of mortality, are intended to remind us of his Untimely Death, which took place about three thousand years after the date commonly assigned to the creation of the world. (S.W. salutes the W.M. as a M.M. and sits.)

sections.heading: Concluding signs and the Royal Arch reference

blocks.text: (The S.D. conducts the Can. to the North/North-East corner of the Lodge and places Can. facing South.)

P. M. - You have already been put into possession of the three ordinary Sign of a Master Mason; I will now intrust you with the remaining two; but for your further instruction I will go through the whole five. This (P.M. demonstrates) is the Sign of Horror; this (P.M. demonstrates) is the Sign of Sympathy; this (P.M. demonstrates) is the Penal Sign. The fourth is the Sign of Grief and Distress. The origin of this Sign was the gesture made by Hiram Abif when after the second blow he made his way from the North to the East Entrance of the Temple, when his distress and agony were so great that the sweat and blood stood in great drops upon his fore- head, and he used this Sign (P.M. demonstrates) as a temporary alleviation of his sufferings. There is another Sign of Grief and Distress said to be in use in certain countries on the Continent of Europe, and which may be useful to a Brother who may happen to be in danger or difficulty in any of those countries. It is given by Clasping the Hands together thus with the Palms outwards, the Hands raised to the Forehead and exclaiming aloud in the language of the country, ‘Come to my assistance, ye Sons of the Widow’ You have already been informed that Hiram Abif was the Son of a Widow of Tyre and as we all masonically claim brotherhood with Hiram Abif so we may all be designated Sons of the Widow.

The fifth in order is the Grand and Royal Sign. It had its origin at the time when the Queen of Sheba, attended by her brilliant retinue, went to view the buildings of the Temple, when they were all so struck by their exceeding magnificence, that raising their Hands above their Heads and bringing the Palms together in the Oriental manner (thus), they exclaimed as with one voice, ‘Oh, Wonderful Masons’
(At a signal from the P.M. the W.M. gives one knock follow by the S.W. and J.W.)
W. M. - To order, Brethren. (the brethren all rise)

P. M. - But King Solomon and those who were present with him, in humble acknowledgment that that great and holy work had been carried on and completed, only through the guidance and the strengthening power of the Almighty; and desiring to ascribe to Him alone the praise and honour and glory, raised their hands in like manner, and exclaimed in unison, 'All Glory to the Most High.'
(All the Brethren accompany the W.M. in act and in word.)
W. M. - Brethren, be seated.
(The S.D. conducts the Can. to the front of the W.M.’s pedestal.)

W. M. - (to Can.) This is the conclusion of the Third Ceremony. At the expiration of a full month, or at any time after that period, you may, if you wish it, be admitted to the Degree of the Holy Royal Arch, the only Degree above the Craft that is recognised by, and is under the sanction of, the Grand Lodge of England.
(S.D. places Can. one pace back and instructs Can.)

S. D. - You will salute the W.M. as a M.M. (Can. does so and S.D. conducts the Can. to any seat in the Lodge except the East. The Deacons return to the respective positions, place the wands in the stands and sit in unison.)
END OF THE CEREMONY OF THE THIRD DEGREE

blocks.text: The Ceremony of Closing the Lodge in the Third Degree. ( short closing to First Degree )
(The W. M. rises and gives one knock with his gavel which is answered by the Wardens.)
W. M. - Brethren, assist me to close the Lodge in the Third Degree. (All rise.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, (J.W. responds with step and sign of M.M.) what is the constant care of every Master Mason?
J. W. - To prove the Lodge close tyled.
W. M. - You will direct that duty to be done. (J.W. discharges sign.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. responds with step and sign of M.M.) you will prove the Lodge close tyled.
(The I.G. discharges sign, goes to the door and gives the 3rd Degree knocks, which are answered by the Ty.)
I. G. (with step and sign of M.M. )
Bro. Junior Warden, the Lodge is close tyled. (I.G. discharges sign.)
J. W. (with step and sign of M.M. )
Worshipful Master, the Lodge is close tyled. (J.W. discharges sign.)
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, (S.W. responds with step and sign of M.M.) what is our next care ?
S. W. - To see that the Brethren appear to order as Master Masons.
W. M. - Brethren, to order in the Third Degree. (All stand to order.)

W. M. - Brethren, by the powers invested in me, I close this Master Masons degree and resume labour in the First Degree. (At the word ‘close’, all the Brethren drop the sign in unison with the W.M. He gives the knocks of the First Degree.)
(W,M. gives the First Degree knocks, followed by the S.W., J.W., I.G. and the Ty.)
I.P.M. goes to the W.M.’s pedestal, kneel on his left knee and conceal both points of the Compasses. I.P.M. salutes the W.M. as an E.A. and returns to his seat.)
The Ceremony of Closing the Lodge.
(The W.M. rises and gives one knock which is answered by the S.W. and the J.W.)
W. M. - Brethren, assist me to close the Lodge. (All rise.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, (J.W. responds with and holds the sign of E.A.) what is the constant care of every Freemason?
J. W. - To prove the Lodge close tyled.
W. M. - You will direct that duty to be done. (J.W. discharges the sign of E.A.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. responds with and holds the sign of E.A.) you will prove the Lodge close tyled.
(The I.G. discharges sign of E.A. and gives the 3 knocks, which are answered by the Tyler.)
I. G. - (with step and sign of E.A.) Bro. Junior Warden, the Lodge is close tyled
. J. W. - (rises with step and sign of E.A.) Worshipful Master, the Lodge is close tyled.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, (S.W. responds with and holds the sign of E.A.) what is our next care ?
S. W. - To see that the Brethren appear to order as Freemasons. (S.W. discharges the sign of E.A.)
W. M. - Brethren, to order as Freemasons.
(All stand to order as E.A.) W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, your constant place in the Lodge?
S. W. - In the West.
W. M. - Why are you so placed?

S. W. - As the sun sets in the West to close the day, so the Senior Warden is placed in the West to close the Lodge by the Worshipful Master's command, after having seen that every Brother has had his due.

Chaplain - Brethren, before the Lodge is closed, let us with all reverence and humility express our gratitude to The Great Architect Of The Universe for the favours which we have received, and may He continue to preserve our Order by adorning its members with every moral and social virtue. So Mote It Be.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, the labours of the day being ended, you have my command to close the Lodge.
(W.M. maintains the sign ; gives one knock with the left hand.)
S. W. - Brethren, by command of the Worshipful Master, I close the Lodge.

(At the word ' close,' all drop the sign in unison. The S.W. gives one knock. The J.D. goes to the Secretary’s table and the S.D. goes to the J.W.’s pedestal. I.P.M. goes to the centre of the Lodge under the ‘G’. Deacons cross their wands with a click to signal the I.P.M. to walk to the W.M.’s pedestal escorted by the Deacons with wands crossed. I.P.M. kneel on his left knee and close the V.S.L. and place the Square and Compasses on it. I.P.M. gives a court bow to the W.M. and returns to his seat. Both Deacons give court bow and return to their respective positions and place their wands in the stands. J.D. closes the first degree tracing board and S.D. puts out the candle on W.M.’s pedestal. S.W. and J.W. put out their candles and S.W. lowers his column to a horizontal position.)
J. W. - And it is closed accordingly until the fourth Wednesday in the ensuing month, except in case of emergency, of which due notice will be given.
(J.W. gives one knock, followed by the I.G. and the Tyler. J.W. raises his column to an upright position.)
I. P. M. (steps down to the floor of the Lodge in front of the W.M.’s pedestal and places his right hand on the closed V.S.L.)

Brethren, nothing now remains but, according to ancient custom, that each Brother lock up the secrets of the Lodge in the safe and sacred repository, the heart, uniting in the act of Fidelity, Fidelity, Fidelity (all give sign of fidelity 3 times), and may God be with us all. So Mote It Be.

(All Brethren remain standing while the D. of C. leads the J.D. from his position, follow by the S.D. taking his position on the J.D.’s left, then the J.W. taking his position behind the Deacons, then the S.W. taking his position on the J.W.’s left and then the W.M. taking his position behind the Deacons and in front of the Wardens. blocks.text: The ceremonies distinguish tools used in building from the moral lessons assigned to them in speculative Masonry. This guide follows the supplied interpretations rather than adding an invented secret meaning.

The first degree discusses time, conscience and education; the second discusses moral conduct, equality and uprightness; the third connects the skirret, pencil and compasses with a straight course of conduct, accountability and limits.

East, west and south, the movement of the sun, the square and compasses, the apron and the corner stone organize the supplied ceremonial explanations. Literal geography, scriptural reference and moral metaphor should not be collapsed into one historical claim.

The Hiram narrative makes fidelity, loss and mortality central to the third degree. The five points of fellowship are explained as mutual assistance and lawful confidentiality; the source itself excepts crimes from that confidentiality.

sections.heading: Start with the claim, not the whole web

blocks.text: Choose one statement with identifiable actors, dates and actions. Find the original document, understand what it actually says, and check whether independent evidence supports the conclusion. Hundreds of neighboring names do not strengthen an unsupported connecting arrow.

Keep four distinctions visible: the creator’s work, the creator’s interpretation, the evidence for a particular statement, and the reader’s unanswered question. A primary source for an artwork is not necessarily an evidential source for its allegations.

Documented record means an identifiable record supports the particular event. Religious or symbolic interpretation describes meaning within a tradition. Hypothesis or speculation describes a proposal not established by the supplied evidence. Unsupported allegation means the upload does not substantiate the accusation. Contradicted or fabricated is used where specific reliable evidence justifies that stronger conclusion.

For example, the Senate hearing is evidence for historical MKUltra investigations. It does not validate every mind-control narrative. The Protocols of the Elders of Zion is an antisemitic fabrication, not a missing document that would prove collective Jewish control.

formula.name: Opening/closing average inventory
formula.expression: (Opening inventory + closing inventory) / 2
inputs: Opening/closing inventory: matching stock definitions.
formula.scope: Two snapshots can miss seasonality; use more observations where needed.
original: Average Inventory = (Beginning Inventory + Ending Inventory) / 2
Amount of inventory a company has on-hand during a period

formula.name: Inventory days on hand
formula.expression: Average inventory / period COGS × period days
inputs: Average inventory: relevant stock base.
COGS and days: matched reporting period.
formula.scope: The source uses period COGS but always multiplies by 365. Use matching period days.
original: Days on Hand (DoH) = (Average Inventory for period / CoGS for period) x 365
DoH is the average days before inventory is sold

references.title: ACCA: performance appraisal and working-capital ratios

formula.name: Stock-to-sales ratio
formula.expression: Stated inventory value / matching sales value
inputs: Inventory: date and valuation basis.
Sales: period and gross/net basis.
formula.scope: Inventory at cost divided by sales at selling prices is a stated operating convention, not a like-cost fraction.
original: Stock to Sales Ratio = Inventory value / Sales value
Is the measurement of the inventory amount in storage versus the number of sales

formula.name: Inventory carrying-cost rate
formula.expression: (Service + risk + capital + storage costs) / stated inventory value
formula.units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
inputs: Costs: matching-period costs included in the carrying-cost scope.
Inventory value: declared average/closing valuation base.
formula.scope: State period and avoid double-counting capital/financing/storage costs. Not every cost category is an accounting expense.
original: Cost of Carry = (Inventory Service Costs + Inventory Risk Costs + Capital Cost + Storage Cost) / Total Inventory Value
Percentage of total inventory value a company pays to maintain inventory in storage

formula.name: Source order-backlog rate
formula.expression: Undeliverable orders / total relevant orders
formula.units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
inputs: Undeliverable orders: orders meeting a declared delayed/backordered definition.
Total orders: matching cohort of orders.
formula.scope: Define backordered versus cancelled or otherwise undeliverable orders; do not mix order counts and units.
original: Backorder Rate = Number of Undeliverable Orders / Total Number of Orders
Tracks the number of delayed orders due to stockouts

formula.name: Sell-through on receipts
formula.expression: Units sold / units received
formula.units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
inputs: Units sold/received: same product, period and unit basis.
formula.scope: This source receipts-based convention differs from available-stock measures when opening stock exists.
original: Sell-through Rate = Number of units sold / Number of units received
Comparison of the inventory amount sold and the amount of inventory received from a manufacturer

formula.name: Inventory scrap-cost ratio
formula.expression: Period scrap expense / average inventory value
formula.units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
inputs: Scrap expense: cost written off for scrap in the period.
Average inventory value: compatible stock valuation.
formula.scope: This is a cost/value measure, not scrap units divided by production units.
original: Scrap Rate = Scrap expenses over the period / Average inventory over the period
Measures the quality of the inventory and is used to decrease the non quality costs

formula.name: Stock-receiving process time
formula.expression: Validation time + recording time + storage-preparation time
inputs: Component times: non-overlapping elapsed/labour times under one declared convention.
formula.scope: Parallel work and elapsed versus labour time can prevent simple addition unless the process definition supports it.
original: Time to receive = Time for stock validation + Time to add stock to records + Time to prep stock for storage
Measures the effeciency of stock receiving process

formula.name: Book-to-physical inventory difference
formula.expression: Book inventory value − physical inventory value
inputs: Book value: ledger stock value.
Physical value: counted stock valued on the same basis.
formula.scope: A negative difference is an overage under this sign convention. A discrepancy alone does not prove fraud.
original: Inventory Shrinkage = Ending inventory value - Physically counted inventory value
Measures the shrinkage due to damage, miscounts and fraud

formula.name: Dead-stock share
formula.expression: Unsellable relevant stock / total relevant available stock
formula.units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
inputs: Numerator/denominator: both units or both values at a matching date and scope.
formula.scope: State obsolescence criteria and snapshot/cohort definitions; do not mix unit and currency bases.
original: Dead Stock = Amount of unsellable stock in period / Amount of available stock in period
Dead stock inventory no one wants to buy. Measures efficiency of supply chain

Some source labels such as “unattributable” and “IP on lease agreement” are incomplete and need transaction-specific interpretation.

blocks.text: Definitions
Intangible asset is an identifiable non~monetary asset without physical substance controlled by the entity from which future economic benefits are expected to flow to the entity
Amortisation is the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an intangible asset over its useful life.
An asset is a resource: (a) controlled by an entity as a result of past events; and (b) from which future economic benefits are expected to flow to the entity.
Carrying amount is the amount at which an asset is recognised in the statement of financial position after deducting any accumulated amortisation and accumulated impairment losses thereon
Cost is the amount of cash or cash equivalents paid or the fair value of other consideration given to acquire an asset at the time of its acquisition or construction

Development is the application of research findings or other knowledge of a plan or design for the production of new or substantially improved materials, devices, products, processes, systems or services before the start of commercial production or use.
Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date
Research is an original and planned investigation undertaken with the prospect of gaining new scientific or technical knowledge and understanding.

Useful life is: (a) the period over which an asset is expected to be available for use by an entity; or (b) the number of production or similar units expected to be obtained from the asset by an entity.
Measurement after initial recognition

items: Cost modelAfter initial recognition, an intangible asset shall be carried at its cost less any accumulated amortisation and any accumulated impairment losses.

Revaluation modelAfter initial recognition, an intangible asset shall be carried at a revalued amount, being its fair value a! the date of the revaluation less any subsequent accumulated amortisation and any subsequent accumulated impairment losses. For the purpose of revaluations under this standard, fair value shall be measured by reference to an active market. Revaluations shall be made with such regularity that at the end of the reporting period lht' carrying amount of the asset does not differ materially from its fair value.

blocks.text: IP carrying amount is increased

Increase shall be recognised in equity under the heading of revaluation surplus. However, the increase shall be recognised in P&L to the extent that it reverses a revaluation decrease of the same asset previously recognised in P&L.
IP carrying amount is decreased
Decrease shall be recognised in P&L. However, the decrease shall be recognised in other comprehensive income to the extent of any credit balance in the revaluation surplus in respect to that asset
